source.author: lucr
source.text: sudabant etiam fauces intrinsecus atrae sanguine et ulceribus vocis via saepta coibat atque animi interpres manabat lingua cruore debilitata malis, motu gravis, aspera tactu.
source.text_original: sudabant etiam fauces intrinsecus atrae / sanguine et ulceribus vocis via saepta coibat / atque animi interpres manabat lingua cruore / debilitata malis, motu gravis, aspera tactu.
source.text_english: Their throats too were sweating within, black with blood and sores; the passage of the voice was blocked and closed up, and the tongue, interpreter of the mind, dripped with gore, weakened by the gums, sluggish in movement, rough to the touch.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: itaque uiator ille uerus ac iustus non dicet illud Lucilianum: homini amico et familiari non est mentiri meum, sed etiam inimico atque ignoto existimabit non esse mentiri suum nec aliquando committet ut lingua interpres animi a sensu et cogitatione discordet.
reuse.text_original: itaque uiator ille uerus ac iustus non dicet illud Lucilianum: homini amico et familiari non est mentiri meum, sed etiam inimico atque ignoto existimabit non esse mentiri suum nec aliquando committet ut lingua interpres animi a sensu et cogitatione discordet.
reuse.text_english: Therefore that true and just traveler will not say that Lucilian line, It is not my business to lie to a friend and acquaintance, but he will also judge it not his place to lie to an enemy and a stranger, and he will never allow that the tongue, the interpreter of the mind, should be at variance with feeling and thought.
